Interface IToolHandler

All Known Implementing Classes:
BaseToolHandler, DefaultToolHandler, MapToolHandler, PlotToolHandler
public interface IToolHandler
Callback interface for toolbar tools.

This interface is intentionally "gesture-first": wherever a tool is driven by a pointer gesture (press/drag/release, rubberbanding, hover move), the callback receives a GestureContext. This keeps signatures uniform and makes it easy to extend tools without proliferating parameter combinations.

Hit testing

The handler provides hit-testing so applications can map canvas points to domain objects (items, nodes, handles, etc.).

One-shot actions

Even one-shot actions (zoom in/out, print, delete...) receive a GestureContext so handlers always have access to toolbar, canvas, and a representative point.

    • createRadArc

      void createRadArc(GestureContext gc, Point[] vertices)
      Create a radial arc.

      The expected interpretation of vertices is tool-defined; for a typical radial arc gesture:

      • vertices[0] = center
      • vertices[1] = radius leg endpoint
      • vertices[2] = angle-defining point
      Parameters:
      gc - gesture context (non-null)
      vertices - gesture vertices (non-null)
